claims.text: Every build method receives a BuildContext, a handle to the location of the widget in the widget tree.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: BuildContext ('A handle to the location of a widget in the widget tree')

claims.text: Navigator.of(context) returns the nearest Navigator ancestor of the given context; MaterialApp creates a Navigator.
claims.source_hint: Flutter API docs: Navigator.of, MaterialApp (WidgetsApp builds a Navigator)

claims.text: Navigator.of with a context that has no Navigator ancestor (e.g. above MaterialApp) fails instead of finding one.
claims.source_hint: Flutter SDK navigator.dart (Navigator.of assert: 'Navigator operation requested with a context that does not include a Navigator')

claims.text: Theme.of(context) looks up the theme provided by an ancestor in the same way.
LoginScreen awaits apiClient.login, returns if !mounted, then calls Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement to CreateOrderScreen.
State.mounted is true while the State object is in the tree; after the widget is removed, its context should not be used.
ProductListScreen's constructor takes only an ApiClient; DonHangApp's build context is above the MaterialApp it returns.
Looking up ancestors through context avoids passing things like the navigator down through every constructor.

self_check.notes: Outline retargeted to stage-1 (DECISIONS.md §3). No InheritedWidget internals; `mounted` explained in one sentence only, per depth_notes.
